Tenure

The field that gets Phuket brochures into trouble, so it is set out as what is stated and what is proven, separately.

Lister's statement

Foreign freehold quota. The tenure check read the listing's detail page and recorded the sale quota as foreigner quota. That is what the lister states about the property, not what the deed records.

Only 8 of the 47 listings checked on this sweep stated tenure at all, so a stated quota is unusually specific for this market — and still unverified.

Not established

Nobody has read the title deed, the quota certificate or the building permit for this property. Whether the structure transfers separately from the land has not been established, and transferability has not been stated at all.

Foreign freehold in a Thai condominium building runs against a 49% quota that can be full. For a villa on land, foreign freehold of the land is not available at all, so the structure of any "foreign freehold" offer needs reading before it is repeated. Take Thai legal advice.

Photography

A photographer has supplied a Drive folder labelled L43, created on 1 June 2026 and shared on 2 September 2026. It is attached to the desk record.

Before this goes to a buyer

In order. The first two decide whether there is anything to sell.

  • Speak to the owner. There is no instruction. Confirm the property is still available, at what price, and on what terms Two Coasts may introduce a buyer.
  • Read the title deed. Establish what the stated foreign quota actually is, in writing, and whether the building transfers with it. Thai counsel, not the lister.
  • Confirm the area basis. The source does not say whether 567.3 sq.m is internal, built-up or total. The price per sq.m inherits that assumption, so check it against the building permit before any rate goes into a comparison.
  • Ask why it has been listed since June 2024. Two years and two months on a portal is the single most useful question to put to the owner.
  • Review the photography for subject and for identifiable people, then republish this page with the frames embedded.
  • Establish the running costs. No common-area maintenance charge, sinking fund or completion record is on file.

About this document. Compiled from structured listing facts collected from PropertyScout on 1 September 2026, under the desk reference L43. Statements marked as the lister's have not been independently verified. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice, and no figure is a projection of what this property will earn.

On tenure. Foreign freehold of land is not available in Thailand. Where a villa is offered on a lease, Thai law registers that lease for a maximum of 30 years; any longer term is a contractual renewal option granted by the lessor, not a registered right, and its enforceability against a future landowner is unsettled. Request the title deed and the registered lease, and take Thai legal advice, before relying on any tenure statement.
